learning_outcomes.text: Possess essential notions on the physical principles underlying the operation of simple solid-state electronic devices.

Know the fundamental characteristics of the most used solid-state devices in electronics (diodes, MOSFET and BJT transistors), and be able to highlight their similarities and differences from the point of view of terminal characteristics.
Know the classification of amplifiers from the point of view of input-output characteristics, and the main circuit configurations of BJT and MOSFET based amplifiers.
Know some fundamental applications of MOSFETs in the field of circuits for processing and storing logic signals.
Know the properties of Operational Amplifiers and some fundamental circuits based on them.
Be able to illustrate the theoretical and technical reasons underlying the properties of fundamental analog and digital circuits.
Be able to analyze simple electronic circuits using diodes and MOSFET or BJT transistors, using the most appropriate models of these devices depending on the intended application for the circuit.

Be able to predict the electrical behavior of simple circuit configurations known in the literature, whether for digital or analog applications, resorting, where necessary, to DC analysis, small-signal sinusoidal regime, or large signals.

Be able to analyze some fundamental circuits based on Operational Amplifiers, single-stage or multi-stage, or, starting from them, appropriately dimension the passive components to obtain assigned specifications in terms of amplification or input and output resistance.

syllabus_topics: General amplifier models and characteristic parameters
The Operational Amplifier (OpAmp): simplified model and fundamental OpAmp circuits (inverting, non-inverting, summing, integrator, differentiator)
The p-n junction: potential barrier, junction capacitance
Characteristic parameters of real logic circuits
Synthesis of static CMOS logic networks
Introduction to signal acquisition and processing using simple programmable systems
teaching_methods: Practical exercises (numerical and using circuit simulators or simple programmable systems)
assessment_rules: The exam consists of an oral examination.
